# AquaShield

> AquaShield detects and localizes leaks in complex pipe networks using non-invasive sensors and AI.

AquaShield (legal entity AquaShield AI Inc., offices at 500 Sansome Street, San Francisco, CA 94111, and Technoparkstrasse 1, 8005 Zurich) builds proprietary clamp-on ultrasonic flow sensors, its own machine learning models that learn a building's normal flow, and a digital twin that narrows a leak to a riser or a building section. Alerts are reviewed with the maintenance team. Founded by robotics researchers Paul Beckers (CEO) and Marguerite Benoist (CTO) with Tim Baumeister (customers and operations). Y Combinator, spring 2026. Developed with MIT Facilities. Live in 25+ buildings in Europe and the US.

## Facts

- Install: 30 seconds per sensor, no pipe cutting, non-invasive
- Scale: built to roll out across a whole portfolio
- Localization: hours instead of weeks or months
- Cost per leak event: about $89k down to about $2k, in AquaShield's simulations
- Localization: to the riser or building section, not the pipe segment
- No accuracy figures published yet
- Languages: English, German (/de/), French (/fr/)
